_comment: Guardrail configuration for the guardrail repo itself. There are no databases, deploys or environments here: the risks are three others, written below. The lists add up to the hook defaults, which already mark as production the commands that contain 'prod', 'produzione' or 'live'.
_prod_mcp_servers: While working on this repo there is no reason to modify real infrastructure. Azure stays readable (get_*, list_*), but every write is blocked instead of asking for confirmation: in auto mode a confirmation is granted on its own.
_prose_mcp_servers: The Docs connector only writes documents: a text that talks about production is not a change to production. On 2026-10-05 it blocked the document on the Sonnet/Opus comparison. The identifiers of its calls stay checked. Added by the user's decision, on 2026-10-06.
_prod_patterns: Empty on purpose: this repo has no environments. The hook defaults are enough, and adding here the example hosts from the documentation (db-production.example.com, appdb) would make every command that touches services/ or tests/ suspicious.
_deny_commands: 1) dangerous.sh is a fixture: it exists to be READ by the hook when someone invokes it, and it contains an rsync --delete towards a remote host. Invoking it today is only a confirmation, and in auto mode the agent grants the confirmation. The rule fires only when the fixture is executed (also with bash/sh, sudo, timeout, source, absolute path), not when the path appears as text: on 2026-10-04 it had blocked a printf that quoted it inside a test JSON. 2) GUARDRAIL_DISABLE= switches the hook off: it is a human decision, taken outside the session. Reading it (printenv GUARDRAIL_DISABLE) stays allowed, /guardrail:check needs it.
_ask_commands: The marketplace installs the plugin from GitHub, branch main: a push here updates the hook code that will run on the machines of everyone who has guardrail installed. It is not just any commit, and it is right to pause for a moment.
_allow_commands: Empty, and may it stay empty: it is the exception that switches the rules off. If one day an entry is needed, it must be justified in the commit that introduces it.
